purpose: Single source of truth for the packages every lakehouse Spark job submits with. The Iceberg version lived in twelve files before this one existed, so raising it meant editing twelve places and nobody ever did: the deployment sat on 1.6.1 while five releases went by.

iceberg.minimum_version_reason: Before 1.8.0 the vectorized Parquet reader corrupts native memory: apache/iceberg#12178, 'Incorrect Results and SIGSEGV on Read', fixed in 1.8.0. Measured on this deployment 2026-08-29 against silver.building_register_units with vectorization on and nothing else changed: 1.6.1 died with SIGSEGV, 1.11.0 read the table. The three tables above ten million rows all died; the two in the low thousands did not, which is why it stayed hidden until a compaction run touched a large table. Root ADR-0064.
iceberg.scope: Iceberg's own storage layer. iceberg-aws-bundle backs S3FileIO, which is how Iceberg reads and writes the files of its tables. It is not the filesystem Spark reads a plain file through, which is what the hadoop block below is for.

hadoop.version_reason: Must equal the Hadoop the Spark image already carries. Measured 2026-08-31 by listing /opt/spark/jars in apache/spark:3.5.6-scala2.12-java17-python3-ubuntu: hadoop-client-api-3.3.4.jar and hadoop-client-runtime-3.3.4.jar. A different hadoop-aws brings a second copy of classes the runtime already defines.
hadoop.scope: The `s3a://` filesystem, so `spark.read` can open an object that is not part of an Iceberg table — the Silver handoff JSONL a load consumes. That image ships no aws, s3, or hadoop-cloud jar at all: 252 jars, none of them. Without this, `spark.read.json("s3a://...")` fails on the scheme while the same job writes Iceberg tables to the same bucket, because those two go through different code.

spark.artifact_suffix_reason: The Iceberg runtime artifact name embeds both, so the artifacts above are only valid for this pair.

r2_read.reason: How every Spark and JVM read of R2 survives a reset connection, written once (root ADR-0102): drop pooled connections before R2 does (TTL, max idle), ask a broken read again after equal-jitter exponential backoff (retries, min and max wait), and let a failed task run again (local[N,task_max_failures], because plain local[N] ignores spark.task.maxFailures). lakehouse_engine reads it for the Iceberg S3FileIO catalog settings, the Hadoop s3a settings and the master URL; foundation-outbox's Rust read policy carries the same numbers and a test holds them equal. Why the task retry is the one that matters for a broken body: Iceberg's S3InputStream (1.11.0, and still on main after 1.12.0) retries only its streaming read() and only on SSL/socket-timeout/socket exceptions, and readFully(position, ...), the ranged read Parquet uses, has no retry at all; the s3.retry settings retry the SDK request up to its response headers, not the body read after it. A body cut short (2026-10-17 lineage stewardship: ConnectionClosedException, Premature end of Content-Length delimited message body, 3,208,879 of 77,287,406 bytes, in S3InputStream.readFully) therefore fails the task, and only the task's own re-run reads the range again; that job ran on plain local[4], so the one failure ended it.
